Our octonion multiplication encoded in ([\[C\]](#C){reference-type="ref" reference="C"}) is such that $e^4$ is treated as a preferred element, and so we choose $u=e^4$ and $J= E^4$. sections.title: The octonionic model for Spin(11,3)
sections.extract: The octonionic model for Spin(11, 3) We now put the O, ˜O building blocks together, and construct an octonionic model for the group Spin(11, 3). The construction we are to describe applies to a more general set of pseudo- orthogonal groups, and so we give it in full generality.

sections.extract: As we already said, the Higgs field $\Phi$ cannot break the ${\rm U}(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry. One thus needs additional Higgs fields.
